title: Hackers used autonomous AI agents to attack Taiwan. Is this the future of cyberwarfare?
facts: Hackers deployed an autonomous artificial intelligence system to conduct cyberattacks against Taiwanese government agencies.
The AI agents mapped 21 Taiwanese government systems over a four-day period in July.
The AI system compromised 85 Taiwanese government user accounts during the cyberattack.
The AI system extracted 2,500 personnel records from Taiwanese government systems.
Israeli AI cybersecurity firm Dream first discovered the autonomous cyberattack on Taiwan.
Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs stated the cyberattack utilized a hybrid approach combining conventional operations with AI agents such as OpenClaw.
The hacker system coordinated up to eight AI agents to execute intrusions without human intervention.
Kenny Huang serves as chairman of the Taiwan Network Information Center.
Amir Becker serves as chief business and strategy officer at the AI firm Dream.
The autonomous cyberattack targeted Taiwan's nuclear safety agency and government IT vendors.
The cyberattack targeted at least seven energy sector companies in Taiwan.
Internal documents linked to the cyberattack contained simplified Chinese text.
Taiwan experienced an average of 2.6 million cyberattacks per day from China in the previous year.
Daily cyberattacks from China against Taiwan increased by 6% compared to 2024.
The Financial Times first reported the autonomous AI cyberattack on Taiwan.
